supplemental_checks.finding: The keyboard can reach and activate Preferences, but focus does not scroll the horizontal nav, leaving text and its focus outline clipped at 390px.

supplemental_checks.command: python inline Playwright probe: 390x844; mouse.move to .primary-nav center; mouse.wheel(350,0)
python inline Playwright probe: 390x844; press Tab six times to Preferences; press Enter

findings.source_clause: Original brief: “desktop and 390px narrow keyboard/pointer operation and horizontal overflow/scroll access” and “Visible internal scrolling is not automatically a defect; verify all controls accessible.”

target_source.evidence: The primary navigation includes the Preferences link to #settings.
At widths under 680px, the nav is a horizontal auto-overflow flex scroller and links do not shrink.

findings.observed: At 390x844, six Tab presses focus Preferences while nav.scrollLeft remains 0. The link right edge is 418.125px while the nav right edge is 374px; its text and focus ring are clipped. Enter activates the link and changes the fragment to #settings. A 350px horizontal pointer wheel scroll moves nav.scrollLeft to 44 and reveals Preferences within the nav.
findings.limits: The control remains keyboard reachable and activatable, and pointer scrolling works. This finding is limited to full visual visibility of keyboard focus in the narrow primary navigation; it is not a claim that the link cannot be used.
